department: Search & Answer Intelligence (department 2): Idris, the Competitor Visibility agent
basis: ADR 0048 (D1-D8 and review rounds 1-5: Idris reads Callum's answers only, never asks an engine; emerging candidates are presence-only until a person confirms them; k <= n and compute() never crashes; client lookalikes are never a candidate, a tracked competitor or a client citation; dismissals cover documented respellings; another tenant's objects are the same 404 as missing ones; nothing of an answer beyond 3 PII-screened excerpts of 160 characters per candidate; a failing Idris never changes Callum's response) and ADR 0046 (Callum). The war room's oracle (shared fold from service-py, WHATWG host reading, A-label decoding, its own dismissal-coverage and reuse rules) judges independently of idris.py.

scenarios.persona: a poisoned answer engine whose answers carry prompt injections promoting a fake brand (with its own domain cited) to the top of the benchmark
scenarios.basis: ADR 0048 D6 / round 4 (an answer holding an injection counts for no candidate), round 1 (emerging never in a share, a leader or a headline before confirmation); seed: the suite's pinned injection

scenarios.persona: answers naming places, people, events, products, publishers, job titles and acronyms in list, pricing and mid-sentence shapes
scenarios.basis: ADR 0048 rounds 2-3 (non-brands are not candidates); seeds: the suite's pinned precision names

scenarios.persona: real-looking brands named and cited by two engines, then confirmed, dismissed, confirmed-then-dismissed or dismissed-then-undone by the owner, the agent or the tenant
scenarios.basis: ADR 0048 round 2 (confirmation is the only way into the shares; a dismissal ends a confirmation), round 1 (undismissal by the owner); seeds: the suite's pinned recall names

scenarios.persona: a new brand cited only through a platform, publisher, institution, shortener, link-in-bio page, Gemini's redirector, a lookalike of the client or a competitor, an IP literal, or a private-suffix / IDN host
scenarios.basis: ADR 0048 D4 (citation owners: a lookalike is never the client or the competitor), round 4 (platforms never candidates), round 5 (shorteners unresolved; PSL private suffixes keep the whole name); seeds: the suite's pinned URLs and hosts

scenarios.persona: answers naming a client lookalike (hyphenated, homoglyph, one edit, legal-suffix, glued) as a provider (then a reviewer confirms every candidate offered), citing a lookalike of the client's domain, the brand's own label, an IDN spelling or a private-suffix host
scenarios.basis: ADR 0048 D6 / round 1 (CLIENT_LOOKALIKE, CLIENT_VARIANT: never a candidate; a lookalike host is never the client); seeds: the suite's pinned lookalike texts

scenarios.persona: the client's own brand respelt (spacing, hyphen, glued, homoglyphs, invisible characters, full-width, legal suffixes) named as a provider with lookalike, IDN or private-suffix domains
scenarios.basis: ADR 0048 D6 / round 1; the names are the ADR's own examples (literal)

seeds.basis: ADR 0048 D6 and review round 1 examples, plus one-edit spellings

scenarios.persona: an owner (or an attacker with the agent's token) tracking the client's own brand or domain, respelt, as a competitor
scenarios.basis: ADR 0048 D8 (422 COMPETITOR_IS_CLIENT), round 1 (excluded at run time: excluded_tracked)

seeds.basis: ADR 0048 D6 / D8 examples; Rival Co is a control

scenarios.persona: answers with 600-item lists, a name repeated 500 times, 400-row tables, 300 headings, 2,000 citations, 100,000 characters of whitespace, nested lists
scenarios.basis: ADR 0048 D5/D6 (25 candidates an answer, 200 a run, 2,000 rows, 3 excerpts of 160, 10 listed, 20 watch), round 5 (k <= n; compute never crashes)

scenarios.persona: competitor sets whose terms overlap (containment, end-start, equal after case / spacing / homoglyph / invisible / full-width folding, against the client's term) so one span could name two brands
scenarios.basis: ADR 0048 round 1 HIGH and round 2 HIGH (422 COMPETITOR_TERMS_OVERLAP; at run time one span names one brand)

scenarios.persona: a dismissed candidate coming back respelt: case, spacing, hyphens, legal suffixes, plurals, 'The ... Network', homoglyphs, full-width, invisible characters, one edit, its domain on another TLD, hyphenated, on a private suffix or a ccSLD; and undocumented respellings
scenarios.basis: ADR 0048 round 1 MED and round 2 (DismissalIndex: key, folded tokens without legal suffixes and plurals, contiguous tokens, one edit for 6+); undocumented respellings are scored SHOULD (dismissed_name_not_on_watch / the oracle decides coverage)

scenarios.persona: callers that may not confirm, dismiss or undo (Compliance, another tenant's hub, a hub without its tenant token, no caller, the agent or the hub undoing), and malformed or foreign keys
scenarios.basis: ADR 0048 D6 / rounds 1-2 (dismiss: owner or tenant; confirm: owner or tenant; undismiss: the owner on the dashboard only; a key must be one seen in the tenant's observations, compact)

scenarios.persona: another tenant's hub or dashboard probing zbm's competitor set, visibility runs, prompt set and domain: exact ids, case and encoding variants, traversal, lists, starting runs
scenarios.basis: ADR 0048 D8 (another tenant's objects answer the same 404 as missing ones; the hub reads its own tenant only and never starts a run)

scenarios.persona: another tenant whose own runs, dismissals and confirmations name the same brand
scenarios.basis: ADR 0048 D6 (look-back over the tenant's own observations for its domain), D8 isolation

scenarios.persona: visibility runs against stale, out-of-window, mismatched (competitor set, prompt-set version, engines), interrupted, unobserved, restricted-era, other-tenant and clock-skewed citation runs
scenarios.basis: ADR 0048 D2 (reuse rules, review round 1: observed_at decides the age) — the oracle's own record of each run decides

scenarios.persona: something happens while a visibility run's citation run is in flight: a second run, a replay of the same request, a dismissal, a confirmation, a competitor-set change, a restriction
scenarios.basis: ADR 0048 D2 (one running citation run per tenant; idempotent by request id; reuse needs the set now in force), D6 (dismissals)

scenarios.persona: 20 tracked competitors (5 terms, 5 domains each) x 50 prompts x 4 engines, dense answers naming many tracked, emerging and lookalike brands
scenarios.basis: ADR 0048 D8 (20 tracked), D5 (2,000 rows), D6 (200 candidates a run, 10 listed); structural bounds only

scenarios.persona: Idris failing while it observes a citation run: its observer cannot be built or raises, observe raises (KeyError, recursion, memory, a kill), returns garbage, its extractor / injection guard / brand matcher / NER raise, recording fails or the ledger refuses
scenarios.basis: ADR 0048 D2 review round 1 (a failing Idris can never change Callum's response, outcome or HTTP status: byte-for-byte against a run without Idris); a run without observations is recorded with no numbers

scenarios.persona: engines failing with every adapter code, refusing, answering ERROR, malformed, crashing, on all calls, half of them, or one engine only
scenarios.basis: ADR 0048 D5 (a failed call is an INCONCLUSIVE row; refusals and failures are excluded from every rate; UNKNOWN never 0%; ENGINE_RUN_STOPPED)

seeds.basis: answer_adapter.CODES and the probe framework's statuses

scenarios.persona: one real adapter (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Perplexity on MockTransport) in a 429 / 5xx / timeout / malformed storm while the others answer
scenarios.basis: ADR 0046 A1-A5 through Callum, ADR 0048 D5 (INCONCLUSIVE rows, UNKNOWN never 0%)

seeds.basis: storm scripts over the driver's Storm steps

scenarios.persona: an answer quoting someone's email, phone, SSN, card number or IP right beside an emerging candidate
scenarios.basis: ADR 0048 D5 (at most 3 excerpts of 160 characters per candidate, PII-screened: withheld when they look like personal data); seeds: the suite's pinned personal-data prompts

scenarios.persona: an engine (or a page it read) putting an API key or a caller / tenant / Andre token beside, before or inside an emerging candidate's name, or in a cited path
scenarios.basis: ADR 0017 W4-5 / ADR 0046 A4 (no key or token in any output) applied to Idris's excerpts and names

scenarios.persona: INVENTED by the war room: random competitor sets and 1-3 runs of hostile answers per engine (markdown, injections promoting a fake brand, client and competitor lookalikes, PSL private and IDN hosts, huge and repeated lists, personal data, failures), with dismissals, confirmations and undismissals between runs (grammar.idris_answers)
scenarios.basis: every MUST above, on inputs nobody listed; terminals from the suite's pinned brand names, injection, personal data and platform URLs

scenarios.persona: INVENTED by the war room: random sequences of visibility runs (random windows and engines), clock moves (also backwards), set and prompt-set changes and reversals, Callum's own runs, interrupted runs, failing observers, restrictions and another tenant's runs (grammar.idris_reuse)
scenarios.basis: ADR 0048 D2 reuse rules: the driver's oracle predicts every reuse from its own record

scenarios.persona: INVENTED by the war room: a dismissed name (pinned or invented) respelt by a random documented or undocumented rule, served on 1-3 later runs, dismissed by the owner, the agent or the tenant (grammar.idris_dismissal)
scenarios.basis: ADR 0048 rounds 1-2 dismissal coverage, judged by the driver's own re-implementation of the documented rule
